resources.string: Save a remote MCP server, test it from TermiNow, then add it to Claude Code in TermiNow or in your Ubuntu. Claude Code keeps using your own login.
Local stdio server, not supported in this release
Profile saved, but its credentials are missing. Edit it to enter them again
Written to %1$s, but Claude Code did not confirm it · %2$s
Disabled: removed from Claude Code, the profile is kept
The test checks the connection from this app only, not from Claude Code in the selected environment.

Allow plain HTTP to MCP servers on this device only (localhost and 127.0.0.1), like a server you run in a terminal while developing it. Everything sent over HTTP, including tokens, is unencrypted. Other servers always need HTTPS with a valid certificate.
Not in this release: local stdio servers, configuring SSH hosts, and OAuth sign-in from TermiNow. For OAuth servers, add them without credentials and sign in with /mcp in Claude Code.
Use letters, numbers, - and _ only, as Claude Code requires
Another MCP server has this name
Saved, leave empty to keep it
Add at least one header, or choose None
Tokens and header values are stored encrypted with a key in the Android keystore and are never shown again. OAuth sign-in is not supported in TermiNow in this release.
No Ubuntu is installed. TermiNow does not install one, use proot-distro in a terminal. SSH hosts are not supported yet.
Each environment has its own home and Claude Code configuration. SSH hosts are not supported yet.
Project directory, in the target environment
Enter the absolute path of the project directory
A shared .mcp.json is often committed to version control, so it can not hold credentials. Use the user or private project scope for this server.
Saved. Configure Claude Code again to use the changes there
Delete the MCP server %1$s from TermiNow?
Delete the MCP server %1$s from TermiNow? It is still in the Claude Code configuration, which this does not change. Disable it first to remove it from Claude Code.
The credentials are also in that file, readable only by its owner.
TermiNow connected from this app. This does not show that Claude Code in %1$s can reach the server: it may have a different network, proxy or certificates. No tool was called.

This server requires OAuth sign-in, which TermiNow does not support in this release, so it could not be tested.\n\nClaude Code can sign in itself: configure the server without credentials, then run /mcp in Claude Code and choose to authenticate.
Check the token or headers of the profile.
Updating the configuration and checking it with Claude Code…
The container %1$s is not installed anymore. TermiNow does not install it.
Claude Code was not found in %1$s.
This Claude Code (%1$s) does not support HTTP MCP servers. Update it first.
The project directory %1$s does not exist in %2$s.
TermiNow can not write %1$s in this environment.
The configuration changed since the preview. Nothing was written, configure again to see the change.
Claude Code did not answer in time.
You can set it up yourself with the manual setup commands.
This updates the entry that TermiNow wrote before.
The entry is already there as it should be. Nothing is written, Claude Code is only asked to confirm it.
The entry is not in the configuration anymore. The server is only marked as disabled.

An entry named %1$s is already there, and TermiNow did not write it or it was changed since:
%2$s

Replace it? A backup is made first.

The entry %1$s was not written by TermiNow or was changed since:
%2$s

Remove it anyway? A backup is made first.
The file is backed up next to it first, and written as a whole so it is never half written. All other settings stay as they are.

Claude Code reads the credentials of a server from its configuration, so they will be stored in %1$s as plain text, readable only by its owner (permissions 600). They are then not only in the encrypted store of TermiNow.

plurals.item: Claude Code is running (%d process). It rewrites ~/.claude.json and could undo this change. Quit it first, or apply anyway and restart it.
Claude Code is running (%d processes). It rewrites ~/.claude.json and could undo this change. Quit it first, or apply anyway and restart it.

resources.string: Claude Code did not list the server. Check its output below.
Claude Code asks to approve servers of a shared .mcp.json the next time it starts in the project.
Claude Code sessions that are already running do not see the change until you restart them, or reconnect the server with /mcp.
Removed the entry from %1$s. Restart running Claude Code sessions.
The entry was not in %1$s anymore. Marked as disabled.
Claude Code still lists a server with this name, from another scope or file.
Nothing is run or written by TermiNow. Run these in a terminal of %1$s:
read -rs keeps the secret out of the screen and the shell history. Claude Code still stores it in its configuration file.
